content.text: {"relation":"MATCH","consensus_summary":"The blind consensus identifies two intertwined dominant readings of barley: (1) humble, lowly provision — the bread of the poor through which God provides (John 6:9; Judges 7:13; 2 Kgs 4:42; Ruth; Rev 6:6) — and (2) the firstfruits grain of the early Passover-season harvest, typologically pointing to Christ's resurrection as 'firstfruits' (Lev 23:10-14; Ex 9:31; 1 Cor 15:20-23). Two responses lead with humility, two lead with firstfruits/resurrection, and all four acknowledge both threads, often noting that teachers combine them.","book_summary":"The book defines barley as 'the firstfruits — the first and humblest grain, reaped in spring; the sheaf waved before the LORD, which is Christ risen,' i.e., the firstfruits/resurrection typology fused with the humility motif.","consensus_core_identification":"Barley = the humble/lowly grain of the poor AND the early firstfruits grain of the Passover-season harvest, typifying Christ risen as the firstfruits (the two threads frequently combined).","book_core_identification":"Barley = the firstfruits, the first and humblest grain, whose waved sheaf is Christ risen.","core_relation":"EQUIVALENT","extension_relation":"SAME_CASES","boundary_disagreement":"None of substance. The book folds both consensus threads (humility and firstfruits/resurrection) into one definition, exactly as the consensus notes many teachers do. It does not exclude cases the consensus admits or add cases it rejects; it simply omits the minority readings (jealousy offering, famine pricing, patristic 'letter of the Law' allegory), which is not a boundary dispute over the core.","material_contradiction":"None. The book's identification is an explicit combination of the two most prominent consensus meanings.","rationale":"The book's core — barley as the first and humblest grain whose wave sheaf typifies the risen Christ as firstfruits — is precisely the pairing the consensus itself flags as the most widely recognizable reading ('the lowly grain that is nonetheless first to be raised/harvested'). Responses B and D give firstfruits/resurrection as primary; A and C give humility as primary with firstfruits as the closely linked companion meaning. Since the book asserts both together and adds nothing that alters the referent's extension, the relationship is a MATCH rather than a refinement.","citation_support":"STRONG","strongest_objection":"One could argue REFINED on grounds that the book elevates the firstfruits/Christ-risen typology to definitional status while much academic commentary treats barley non-symbolically, and that 'humblest' is not directly evidenced by the printed verses. But the consensus explicitly lists firstfruits/resurrection as a common-to-primary reading, so no boundary or extension actually shifts; also Lev 23:10 does not name barley, requiring the Ex 9:31 inference, which slightly weakens the printed-citation chain.","confidence":"high"}
